responds_to.note: The reviewer observed a receipt generation that has since been superseded. This response opens a new sealed generation; see evidence-manifest.json.

findings.finding: .bibi-field-hint used an opacity-only treatment, with no explicit colour and below the readable size floor
findings.why_it_mattered: This text states the password rules, so a reader who cannot resolve it cannot satisfy the field. `opacity` multiplies against whatever surface is behind it, which makes the resulting contrast unknowable rather than merely low — it cannot be checked, only guessed at.
findings.change: Removed `opacity`. Declared an explicit ink colour (#4a4f4c) and raised the size to 0.8rem.

measured_in_browser.threshold: WCAG AA body text is 4.5:1; 0.8rem is 12.8px at the default root size

findings.finding: .bibi-signout.bibi-abandon lacked a 44px minimum, a clear focus-visible state, and adequate padding
findings.why_it_mattered: Secondary is a matter of emphasis, not of size. A control small enough to miss is not a quieter control, it is a broken one — and keyboard users had no visible focus affordance at all.
findings.change: min-height 44px, padding 10px 18px, and a dedicated :focus-visible outline with offset shared with .bibi-signout. Kept transparent background and pill shape so it stays below the primary CTA in hierarchy.

defect_found_by_measurement.what: The first fix declared the padding on a single-class `.bibi-abandon` rule. `.bibi-signout` is declared later at equal specificity, so it won on source order: the source read 10px/18px while the browser resolved 4px/10px.
defect_found_by_measurement.how_found: The pixel measurement disagreed with the stylesheet. A source-level assertion had already passed on the declared value.
defect_found_by_measurement.fix: Selector raised to `.bibi-signout.bibi-abandon`, in the base rule and in the 380px override. A regression test now fails if a single-class `.bibi-abandon` rule reappears.

findings.finding: .bibi-error signalled failure by colour alone and shifted the layout when it appeared
findings.why_it_mattered: Red-green colour blindness is common enough that 'the text turned red' is not a signal, and on a translucent card a tinted sentence reads as ordinary prose. Separately, the message appearing pushed the submit button down and out from under a cursor already moving toward it.
findings.change: The state is now carried by a tinted panel, a 3px leading rule, a 1px border and a `!` glyph that survives greyscale and a failed stylesheet. The glyph is aria-hidden by construction (::before) while the sentence keeps role="alert". A always-present .bibi-error-slot reserves one line's height in both auth forms.

findings.finding: The signed-out shell presented pre-auth operations and navigation as if available
findings.why_it_mattered: The chrome around the sign-in card advertised an office, meetings, a work board and a green 'system healthy' pill to someone who had not authenticated and, in the case of the pill, on the strength of a measurement the browser had never taken.
findings.change: The workspace now reports an auth gate up to the shell through a shared vocabulary in src/bibi/surface.js, defaulting to LOCKED so the first frame cannot flash an open shell. While locked, every destination except the sign-in surface itself is disabled in fact — the DOM `disabled` property, aria-disabled, no click handler at all — and marked with the word 잠김, a not-allowed cursor and reduced emphasis. The status pill reads 로그인 필요 / 인증 후 이용 가능 instead of claiming health.
gates_covered: signed in but password not yet set
findings.signed_in_shell_impact: None. Every lock rule is scoped under .app-shell.is-auth-locked and the gate is only ever consulted on the Bibi surface; a test asserts both.

deliberate_tradeoff.what: Signed out, the legacy Hermes views are no longer reachable from the navigation.
deliberate_tradeoff.why_acceptable: Those views talk to a local Hermes gateway through the dev proxy; in the deployed product there is no such proxy, so they are already non-functional on Production. Locking them signed-out removes an advertisement, not a capability. They remain reachable by explicit ?view= URL for local development.

stale_test_corrected.test: tests/bibiWorkspaceVisual.test.js — 'App derives the Bibi surface from the shared predicate, not a loose string'
stale_test_corrected.was: pinned the exact named-import set: import { isBibiSurface } from "./bibi/surface.js"
stale_test_corrected.failed_because: the import list legitimately grew to carry the auth-gate vocabulary
stale_test_corrected.now: asserts isBibiSurface is imported from the shared module and is what App branches on, regardless of what else is imported alongside
stale_test_corrected.note: The protected property — the surface is derived from the shared predicate rather than a loose string — is unchanged and still asserted.

D3 non-colour cue and reserved space

console_errors.classification: Not product defects. Local: the deliberate 400 from the stub's reject-me@example.invalid route, plus a websocket the stub does not implement. Production: only the 400 from the deliberately rejected sign-in probe, one per viewport.

supabase_auth_state_verified.method: public, unauthenticated readback only — no credential, no CLI write, no config change
supabase_auth_state_verified.how_site_url_was_read_without_credential: /auth/v1/verify validates redirect_to against the allowlist and falls back to site_url when the target is not allowed. A probe with an allowed target confirms the allowlist; a probe with a deliberately foreign target makes the server name site_url itself. Both used a bogus token, so nothing was consumed or created.
supabase_auth_state_verified.improvement_over_prior_generation: The prior receipt recorded site_url and the allowlist as orchestrator-reported and not publicly verifiable. They are now verified directly by this writer.

constraints_observed.vercel_project: existing bibi-workspace-18 only; no project created or reused
